name: How do I choose the right drywall thickness for my project?

mainEntity.name: How do I choose the right drywall thickness for my project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing the correct drywall thickness depends on the application. Standard wall applications typically use 1/2-inch drywall, which provides a good balance of strength and manageability. For ceilings, 5/8-inch drywall is often preferred to prevent sagging, especially if joist spacing is wider. Thicker drywall, such as 5/8-inch, is also required for fire-rated assemblies due to its increased density. This is a decision factor based on structural support, fire safety requirements, and the specific load-bearing or spanning characteristics needed for the installation. Our team can advise on the optimal thickness for your project's longevity and code compliance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose drywall thickness based on application: 1/2-inch for standard walls, 5/8-inch for ceilings or fire-rated assemblies to prevent sagging and meet codes.
